stableMappingPatterns.name: Effective date unadjustedDate copied
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Effective (unadjusted) dates in FpML are repeatedly carried into the CDM effectiveDate.adjustableDate.unadjustedDate element without semantic transformation.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Multiple example trades show identical unadjusted date values preserved in CDM effective date fields, indicating a direct copy rule.
caveats: This addresses the unadjustedDate element specifically; businessDayConvention and adjustment rules may also appear separately in examples.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Termination date unadjustedDate copied
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Termination (unadjusted) dates in FpML are repeatedly carried into the CDM terminationDate.adjustableDate.unadjustedDate element without semantic transformation.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Representative examples consistently preserve the FpML termination unadjusted date in the CDM termination date field, indicating a direct mapping.
caveats: This is specific to unadjustedDate copying; other termination-related metadata (conventions/adjustments) may require additional mapping rules.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Fixed price elements normalized into CDM price structure
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: FpML fixed price, currency and unit elements are repeatedly reshaped into the CDM price object with nested value, currency and per-unit unit normalization.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Multiple fixed-price physical trades show the same normalization pattern: numeric price -> price.value.value, currency -> unit.currency.value, and unit normalized into per-unit capacityUnit.
caveats: Unit normalization mapping (e.g., Gal -> USGAL) is applied in examples; some unit mappings are uncertain or context-dependent.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Option type mapping to payout.optionpayout.optiontype
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Commodity option trades map the FpML option type into the CDM payout.optionPayout.optionType element (e.g., Call/Put -> OptionType).
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: All representative option examples show direct mapping of the option type from the FpML option section into the CDM payout structure.
caveats: This covers option-type value mapping only; other option-specific fields (exercise style, expiries) may need separate handling.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Price fields reshaped and unit normalized
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Fixed-price fields (price, currency, unit) are reshaped into the CDM price structure and units normalized to CDM canonical unit codes.
notes: Example mappings include explicit unit normalization (e.g., Gal -> USGAL).
Mapping assumes a canonical CDM unit vocabulary; some source units require normalization rules.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Spread amount+currency converted to CDM price structure
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Calculation spread amounts with currency are repeatedly converted into the CDM price.value and unit.currency representation.
notes: This converts 'spread' style pricing into the canonical CDM price representation used elsewhere in the folder.
Some spreads are expressed relative to indexes or references and may require additional resolution outside this normalization.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Duplicate tradeIdentifier entries in CDM
variantsAndExceptions.description: Several CDM examples show duplicate tradeIdentifier entries (same assignedIdentifier or tradeId repeated). This is observed across multiple examples and is a deviation from a one-to-one identifier expectation.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Post-processing or de-duplication logic may be required when consolidating CDM trade identifiers; treat duplicate entries as a special case requiring review.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Unit code normalization exceptions
variantsAndExceptions.description: Source unit codes are normalized to CDM canonical codes in examples (e.g., 'Gal' -> 'USGAL'). Other units appear with uncertain mappings (MMBTU -> USMMBTU, Therm -> USTHM) and may require specific rules.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Unit normalization is necessary for price and volume fields. Some source units require explicit mapping rules; absent those rules, canonicalization may be inconsistent across trades.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: meta.globalKey entries generated
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: CDM files repeatedly contain meta.globalKey entries (generated identifiers/defaults) under dateAdjustments.meta.globalKey that are not sourced from FpML.
caution: meta.globalKey entries appear to be generated by CDM tooling; they should not be treated as authoritative mappings from FpML content.
Downstream consumers relying on meta.globalKey should be aware these values may not exist in the source FpML.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: Party identifiers (LEI) added in CDM
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: CDM party.partyId.identifier.value fields often contain LEI or generated identifier values that are not present in the FpML input; these appear to be inserted during CDM creation.
caution: LEI values in the CDM do not have an obvious FpML origin in these examples; treat them as supplied/enriched metadata rather than direct mappings.
If mapping requires authoritative party identifiers, a separate lookup or enrichment source is necessary.
